<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on the earlier explanation, the elevation of Chochmah as it becomes a source for Binah is included within the elevation of Binah, and the plural "miracles for our fathers" refers to elevation in both intellects, including the essence of Chochmah above being a source for Binah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And according to what was explained above</t>
    <t s="2">(section 4)</t>
    <t s="3">—that this [matter] that Chochmah becomes a source for Binah is [considered] nothing relative to the essence of Chochmah</t>
    <t s="4">(it is considered nothing and non-entity)—</t>
    <t s="5">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="6">that the elevation and ascent in the aspect of Chochmah, which becomes a source for Binah,</t>
    <t s="7">is included in the elevation and ascent of Binah23,</t>
    <t s="8">and what is said "miracles for our fathers" in the plural,</t>
    <t s="9">[indicates] that the elevation and ascent through the miracles is in the two intellects, in Binah and in Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="10">the intention in this is that through the miracles an elevation and ascent is made also in the essence of Chochmah, which is above being a source for Binah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>To understand this, we preface that the two opinions (upper knowledge and lower knowledge) are both true because each has its root in the Essence of Ein Sof, and the perfection of lower knowledge is achieved through the illumination of upper knowledge within it.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it will be understood by prefacing what was brought above</t>
    <t s="1">(in the discourse beginning "Patal Eliyahu"24),</t>
    <t s="2">that the two opinions</t>
    <t s="3">(the upper opinion and the lower opinion)</t>
    <t s="4">are true,</t>
    <t s="5">because both of them have a root in the Essence of Ein Sof.</t>
    <t s="6">For that Ein Sof is</t>
    <t s="7">(in revelation)</t>
    <t s="8">below, below, without end, is the root of the upper opinion, that "below is nothing,"</t>
    <t s="9">and that Ein Sof is</t>
    <t s="10">(in concealment)</t>
    <t s="11">above, above, without limit, is the root of the lower opinion, that "below is something."</t>
    <t s="12">And it was explained there25,</t>
    <t s="13">that this—that even the lower opinion is true, because it has a root in the Essence of Ein Sof—</t>
    <t s="14">is</t>
    <t s="15">because the opinion that "below is something" is</t>
    <t s="16">(not</t>
    <t s="17">that relative to this level the lower entity is in itself an existence,</t>
    <t s="18">but rather)</t>
    <t s="19">in order that there should be the revelation of "above, above, without limit."</t>
    <t s="20">And this is that the perfection of the lower opinion is through the illumination of the revelation of the upper opinion shining within it,</t>
    <t s="21">for in externality it appears that the opinion that "below is something" is that the lower entity is in itself an existence,</t>
    <t s="22">and through its connection with the upper opinion it is revealed that its content</t>
    <t s="23">(in internality)</t>
    <t s="24">is the revelation of "above, without limit."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Similarly, regarding the lower opinion in the conduct of nature, the perfection of natural conduct is achieved through drawing down the revelation of that which is above nature, revealing its inner essence as being solely by His will.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And similarly, regarding the matter of the lower opinion in the conduct of nature,</t>
    <t s="1">that this—that the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts every created being according to its nature</t>
    <t s="2">(according to its temperament and characteristics)—</t>
    <t s="3">which indicates that the creations occupy a place, is</t>
    <t s="4">(not that the creations in themselves occupy a place relative to Him,</t>
    <t s="5">but rather)</t>
    <t s="6">because it arose in His will, blessed be He, that there should be a perception of place for the creations.</t>
    <t s="7">And the difference between natural conduct and miraculous conduct is,</t>
    <t s="8">that the will in natural conduct is to conduct the world in a manner that the world is an existence,</t>
    <t s="9">and the will in miraculous conduct is to conduct the world in a manner that the world is considered as nothing.</t>
    <t s="10">And this is that the perfection of natural conduct is through drawing into it the revelation of that which is above nature,</t>
    <t s="11">for specifically through this the inwardness of natural conduct is revealed,</t>
    <t s="12">which is that it is because it arose in His will, blessed be He.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
